stories.headline: OpenAI walks back GPT-5.6 Sol changes and boosts usage after 'nerfing' backlash

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux said on July 13 the company landed inference optimizations for GPT-5.6 Sol and is passing the savings to all subscriptions, expected to yield about 10% more usage on its own.
key_facts.excerpt: We have landed inference optimizations and are passing down savings to all the subscriptions for GPT-5.6 Sol. That should result in around 10% more usage on its own.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI reverted GPT-5.6 Sol's in-product context-size limit from 372k back to 272k tokens after the higher limit caused more usage to be charged than intended, and said it would roll 372k back out in the coming days.
key_facts.excerpt: by changing the context size limit in the product to 372k for GPT-5.6 Sol, up from 272k for GPT-5.5, it resulted in more usage being charged than intended. We have reverted to 272k and will work to roll back out to 372k in the days to come.

key_facts.fact: The company reverted an experiment that had changed reasoning-effort ('juice') values and said it is fixing higher-than-intended multi-agent usage at high and xhigh reasoning effort.
key_facts.excerpt: we ran some experiments where reasoning efforts were changed (referred to as juice values under the hood) and have reverted this. There is slightly more usage of multi-agent than intended in high and xhigh reasoning effort, we are fixing this going forward.

key_facts.fact: The updates followed user complaints on July 13 that GPT-5.6 Sol's 'juice values (thinking budgets)' had been 'severely degraded' compared with release day, with some subscribers threatening to cancel.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.6 Sol's juice values (thinking budgets) have been severely degraded compared to release day ... aaaaaand cancel sub, has been fun while it lasted

key_facts.fact: Sottiaux titled the update 'No nerfing, only good stuff!' and said the temporary suspension of the 5-hour usage limit remains in effect.
key_facts.excerpt: Updates for Codex and ChatGPT Work users. No nerfing, only good stuff! ... And we continue to have the 5h limit temporarily not apply.

sources.title: Tweet by @thsottiaux: Updates for Codex and ChatGPT Work users. No nerfing, only good stuff!
Tweet by @scaling01: aaaaaand cancel sub, has been fun while it lasted

stories.headline: Israel launches NIS 70M bio-AI consortium with NVIDIA and Teva to build models on biological data

key_facts.fact: The Israel Innovation Authority announced on July 12 an investment of about NIS 70 million, with industry partners, to establish the Israel BioToken Factory Initiative (IBFI), a national R&D consortium for the next generation of AI in biology, drug discovery and personalized medicine.
key_facts.excerpt: The Israel Innovation Authority today announced a NIS 70 million investment, together with leading industry partners, in the establishment of the Israel BioToken Factory Initiative (IBFI), a new national research and development consortium that will develop a shared technological infrastructure for the next generation of artificial intelligence applications in biology, drug discovery, and personalized medicine.

key_facts.fact: Consortium partners include NVIDIA, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, Sheba Medical Center, CytoReason, TerraCyte Analytics and MeMed, plus researchers from the Weizmann Institute of Science, the Technion and Ben-Gurion University.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the consortium's partners are NVIDIA, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, Sheba Medical Center, CytoReason, TerraCyte Analytics, and MeMed, alongside leading researchers from the Weizmann Institute of Science, the Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, and Ben-Gurion University of the Negev.

key_facts.fact: The shared platform has two core components: 'Bio Tokens,' a standardized representation layer for different types of biological data, and a 'Factory Model,' a platform to develop, integrate, run and access AI-based biological models.
key_facts.excerpt: The first, Bio Tokens, will provide a standardized representation layer for different types of biological data. The second, Factory Model, will serve as a platform enabling the development, integration, execution, and accessibility of AI-based biological models.

key_facts.fact: The infrastructure aims to connect molecular, cellular, dynamic and clinical data in a single computational framework as pre-competitive infrastructure serving Israel's life-sciences ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: these two components will make it possible to connect molecular, cellular, dynamic, and clinical data within a single computational framework, creating a shared infrastructure that will serve industry, academia, and the healthcare system.

key_facts.fact: Scientific activities are led by Prof. Eran Segal and Prof. Nir Yosef of the Weizmann Institute, Prof. Shai Shen-Orr of the Technion and Prof. Assaf Zaritsky of Ben-Gurion University.
key_facts.excerpt: The scientific activities are led by Prof. Eran Segal and Prof. Nir Yosef of the Weizmann Institute of Science, Prof. Shai Shen-Orr of the Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, and Prof. Assaf Zaritsky of Ben-Gurion University of the Negev.

key_facts.excerpt: Insilico Medicine ... and China Medical System Holdings Limited ('CMS') ... today announced an additional AI-empowered drug discovery collaboration targeting a mass-market indication in central nervous system with an innovative mechanism of action (MoA) identified by PandaOmics.

stories.headline: Apple fast-tracks AI-focused M7 silicon, skips M6 Pro/Max; M7 Ultra to support 1.5TB RAM

key_facts.fact: In his July 12 Power On newsletter, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported Apple is accelerating development of the M7 chip, built around major on-device AI (Neural Engine) upgrades, with the base M7 due in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: it's accelerating development of the M7, which should arrive in the first half of 2027 with significant Neural Engine upgrades.

key_facts.fact: Apple is skipping Pro and Max versions of the upcoming M6 chip, releasing only a base M6 as early as this year, the first time since the M1 that a generation lacks Pro/Max variants.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple will be releasing a regular M6 chip ... M7 Max chips in late 2027, and an M7 Ultra chip in 2028.

key_facts.fact: The M7 Ultra, on track for 2028, is designed to support up to 1.5TB of RAM (double the M5 Ultra) and is expected to be the basis for a new Apple server product.
key_facts.excerpt: The M7 Ultra is expected to be the basis for a new server product from Apple as well, with support for up to 1.5TB of RAM.

key_facts.fact: Apple's Neural Engine, the backbone of its on-device AI, traces back to work done for its abandoned self-driving car program, and the company is now making AI hardware a cornerstone of its strategy.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's self-driving car program never really got off the ground, but it may have been what made the company's chips the powerful AI performers they are.

key_facts.fact: The base M7 is reported to carry around 240GB/s of memory bandwidth, up roughly 56% from the M5's 153GB/s.
key_facts.excerpt: The base M5 chip has 153GB/s memory bandwidth, and the base M7 chip could have 240GB/s bandwidth.

key_facts.excerpt: "Today's groundbreaking marks the start of the second phase, which will include a third and fourth plant," Wu said.

key_facts.fact: TSMC's first advanced packaging plant at Chiayi is already in mass production and its second plant is expected to begin mass production soon.

key_facts.fact: The expansion is aimed at scaling TSMC's advanced packaging capacity, including its chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) technology, as demand from AI chip designers such as Nvidia continues to outstrip supply.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is rapidly expanding its advanced chip-packaging capacity, including its chip-on-wafer-on-substrate technology, as demand from artificial intelligence chip designers like Nvidia continues to outstrip supply.

key_facts.fact: The National Science and Technology Council said the Phase II site would be developed into an advanced packaging industry cluster led by TSMC and connected with other Taiwan science parks to form an AI and semiconductor corridor.

stories.headline: Holiday Robotics raises record ₩155B ($103M) Series A, Korea's largest, for factory humanoid

key_facts.fact: South Korean humanoid startup Holiday Robotics said on July 13 it completed a Series A round worth 155 billion won (about US$103 million), the largest Series A ever raised by a domestic startup and the largest single round by a Korean humanoid specialist.
key_facts.excerpt: Holiday Robotics ... said on the 13th that it has completed a Series A funding round worth 155 billion won. The investment is the largest Series A round ever raised by a domestic startup.

key_facts.fact: Existing backers Stonebridge Ventures, Atinum Investment, Intervest and Springcamp joined, alongside new investors including IMM Investment, KB Investment, Bon Angels, Premier Partners and US-based Goodwater Capital, plus the state-run Korea Development Bank and Industrial Bank of Korea.
key_facts.excerpt: New investors including IMM Investment, SL Investment, KB Investment, Bon Angels Venture Partners ... and Goodwater Capital joined. The Korea Development Bank and the Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) also appeared on the list of investors.

key_facts.fact: The company's flagship robot, FRIDAY, is a wheeled humanoid standing 176 cm tall and weighing 115 kg with 64 degrees of freedom, built for repetitive manufacturing and logistics tasks alongside human workers.
key_facts.excerpt: FRIDAY ... is a wheeled humanoid ... Standing 176 cm tall and weighing 115 kg, it features 64 degrees of freedom (DoF), including its head, arms, hands, waist, and wheels.

key_facts.fact: Holiday Robotics, founded in 2024 by Song Ki-young (founder of industrial AI-vision firm Sualab), plans to commercialize FRIDAY in the second half of 2026, produce 100 units a year initially and scale to 1,000 units annually by 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Holiday Robotics is a physical AI company founded by a CEO who previously built industrial AI vision company Sualab in 2013 ... It aims to reach an annual production capacity of 100 units in 2026 ... then scale to 1,000 units annually in 2027.

key_facts.fact: The company plans manufacturing infrastructure capable of producing more than 10,000 units a year and aims to lower FRIDAY's price to around 100 million won through mass production; it is running proof-of-concept trials with automotive, semiconductor and logistics customers.
key_facts.excerpt: It also plans to build manufacturing infrastructure capable of producing more than 10,000 units annually. In the short term, it has set a goal of lowering the product price to around 100 million won through mass production.

stories.headline: Samsung reaches tape-out on Tesla's AI5 chip, to build it on 2nm at Taylor, Texas fab

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics has begun preparations to manufacture Tesla's next-generation AI5 chip, after a Samsung Foundry executive disclosed on LinkedIn that the Tesla-Samsung AI5 chip had completed its tape-out, its final design step before mass production.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics Co. has begun preparations to manufacture Tesla's next-generation artificial intelligence (AI) chip, known as the AI5 ... a recent LinkedIn post by a Samsung executive ... said Tesla's AI5 chip had completed its tape-out process.

key_facts.fact: The AI5 will be manufactured using Samsung's 2-nanometer process at its plant in Taylor, Texas, and is expected to be integrated into Tesla's next-generation products in the near future; it marks the first time a detailed production timeline for Samsung's AI5 output has emerged.
key_facts.excerpt: the AI5 chip will be manufactured using Samsung's 2-nanometer process at its U.S. plant in Taylor, Texas ... The disclosure marks the first time a detailed production timeline for Samsung's manufacturing of Tesla's AI5 chip has emerged.

key_facts.fact: AI5 is Tesla's custom-designed chip intended to power its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, Optimus humanoid robots and AI data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: AI5 is Tesla's custom-designed chip intended to power the company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, Optimus humanoid robots and AI data centers.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's Taylor foundry is expected to begin initial operations later this year before starting mass production for major customers, including Tesla, in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Taylor foundry is expected to begin initial operations later this year before starting mass production for major customers, including Tesla, in 2027.

key_facts.fact: Producing AI5 on Samsung's 2nm process supports market expectations that Samsung's 2nm yield has surpassed 60%; the engineer, James Kim, deleted the LinkedIn post after it was picked up by news reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Kim's post indicated that the AI5 will be manufactured on the 2-nanometer process, supporting the market assumption that Samsung's 2-nanometer yield has exceeded 60 percent ... He deleted the post after news reports.

stories.headline: Iran hits six Gulf states as US launches third wave of strikes over Hormuz

key_facts.fact: On Sunday, July 12, Iran launched missile and drone attacks on Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, hours after the US carried out a third round of airstrikes on Iran in a week.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran launched missile and drone attacks against Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Jordan and the United Arab Emirates on Sunday, widening its military campaign across the Gulf only hours after the United States carried out a third round of airstrikes against Iranian targets.

key_facts.fact: In Qatar, three people including a child were wounded by falling shrapnel from intercepted Iranian fire; Iran's IRGC said it had targeted the Al Udeid airbase with ballistic missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC said it also targeted Qatar's Al Udeid airbase with ballistic missiles... Three people, including a child, were wounded as a result of falling shrapnel from the interception of Iranian attacks, Qatar's Ministry of Interior said.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz closed 'until further notice', and Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said passage was not currently possible due to US military movements.
key_facts.excerpt: On Saturday night, the IRGC announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz until further notice after attacking a container ship using what it called an unapproved route.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it hit more than 300 military targets across three waves, including coastal surveillance, logistics, communications, and missile, drone and naval assets.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command said more than 300 military targets were hit during three waves, including coastal surveillance, logistics, communications, as well as missile, drone and naval assets.

key_facts.fact: Kuwait's Defense Ministry said three northern land border posts and a Kuwait Oil Company offshore drilling platform were damaged, with one worker wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: Kuwait's Defense Ministry said three 'land border posts' in the north and an offshore drilling platform of the Kuwait Oil Company were damaged, with one worker wounded.

key_facts.fact: Oman's maritime authority rescued 23 crew members from a commercial ship near the strait, with one crew member, described by India as an Indian national, missing.
key_facts.excerpt: Oman's maritime authority said it rescued 23 crew members but one was missing. India's foreign ministry called him an Indian national.

stories.headline: US Senator Lindsey Graham, close Trump ally, dies at 71 of aortic dissection

key_facts.fact: Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, one of President Trump's closest congressional allies, died at 71, his office announced Sunday, July 12, after what it first called a 'brief and sudden illness'.
key_facts.excerpt: Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has died at the age of 71. He died on Saturday evening following a 'brief and sudden illness', according to his office.

key_facts.fact: A preliminary medical examiner finding shared by his office attributed the death to an aortic dissection, a tear in the aorta, related to hardening of his arteries.
key_facts.excerpt: Sen. Lindsey Graham... died after a tear in his aorta, according to a preliminary medical examiner finding shared by his office. The tear in the inner wall of the aorta, called an aortic dissection, was related to the hardening of Graham's arteries.

key_facts.fact: Graham had just returned from Kyiv, where he met Ukrainian President Zelensky on Friday, with no known health concerns before the trip; he had turned 71 two days before dying.
key_facts.excerpt: Graham had just returned from Kyiv, where he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday. There were no known health concerns ahead of his trip.

key_facts.fact: South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster can appoint a temporary replacement until the end of Graham's current term in January, with the seat then contested in November's midterms.
key_facts.excerpt: South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster now has the power to appoint a temporary replacement for Graham until the end of his current term in January.

key_facts.fact: President Trump led tributes, describing Graham, a leading Republican voice on defense and foreign policy, as a 'true American'.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump led tributes to Graham, a leading Republican voice on defense and foreign policy, describing him as a 'true American'.

stories.headline: 25-plus leaders gather in Paris for Coalition of the Willing summit on Ukraine

key_facts.excerpt: France is gearing up to host a meeting of the 'Coalition of the Willing' ahead of this year's 14 July celebrations, with at least 25 heads of state or government due to meet in Paris on Monday to discuss support for Ukraine.

stories.headline: Spanish wildfire in Almeria kills 13 as heatwave-driven blaze is contained

key_facts.fact: A wildfire in Spain's Almeria province (Andalusia), which erupted Thursday, killed at least 13 people after a 93-year-old British woman injured in the fire died in hospital on Sunday, July 12.
key_facts.excerpt: Regional authorities in Andalusia said on Sunday that a 93-year-old British woman injured in the fire had died in hospital, bringing the death toll to 13.

key_facts.fact: The fire was stabilised on Sunday, allowing hundreds of the roughly 1,500 evacuees to begin returning home; around 500 firefighters backed by more than 20 water-dropping aircraft battled the blaze.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 500 firefighters, backed by more than 20 water-dropping aircraft, were battling the blaze... The wildfire -- one of the deadliest in Spain's recent history -- forced some 1,500 people to evacuate.

key_facts.fact: The blaze burned around 7,000 hectares and at its most intense advanced as fast as 100 metres per minute, which officials called an unprecedented level of severity.
key_facts.excerpt: the deadly fire, which has burned an area of around 7,000 hectares since it erupted on Thursday... at speeds of up to 100 metres (330 feet) per minute.

key_facts.fact: Authorities suspect the fire began when a power line broke during an extreme heatwave that pushed temperatures above 40C; most of those killed were foreign nationals who died in vehicles or on foot after trying to flee.
key_facts.excerpt: The authorities suspect the wildfire... began when a power line broke during an extreme heatwave that has pushed temperatures above 40C... the 13 people who died in the fast-moving fire had been trapped in vehicles or tried to flee on foot. Most were foreigners.

key_facts.fact: Two British hikers were found alive but badly burned, with about 40% burns; the fire is among the deadliest in Spain's recent history, striking amid Western Europe's third heatwave in six weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: A British couple have been found down a ravine, badly burned and semi-conscious... They found the couple in critical condition, semi-conscious and with severe burns covering 40% of their bodies.

stories.headline: Eisai and Biogen say at-home Leqembi injection matches IV in early Alzheimer's

key_facts.fact: On July 12, Eisai and Biogen announced data at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC) 2026 in London indicating the Leqembi (lecanemab) subcutaneous autoinjector offers efficacy and safety comparable to intravenous administration in early Alzheimer's disease.
key_facts.excerpt: Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. announced today that new data presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference (AAIC) 2026 in London support that the LEQEMBI (lecanemab) subcutaneous autoinjector (SC-AI) formulation offers efficacy and safety comparable to intravenous (IV) administration for people with early Alzheimer's disease (AD).

key_facts.fact: The data showed once-weekly 500 mg subcutaneous dosing achieved drug exposure similar to the approved IV initiation regimen of 10 mg/kg every two weeks, supporting the expectation of similar clinical efficacy and safety.
key_facts.excerpt: Results showed that once-weekly 500 mg SC-AI achieved drug exposure similar to the approved intravenous (IV) initiation regimen (10 mg/kg every two weeks), supporting the expectation of similar clinical efficacy and safety, independent of the route of administration.

key_facts.fact: The session covered pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, efficacy, safety and real-world patient and care-partner experience data for the subcutaneous formulation, which enables at-home administration rather than IV infusions.
key_facts.excerpt: This session presented data from the lecanemab SC-AI development program in early Alzheimer's disease, including pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), efficacy, safety and real-world patient and care partner experience findings.

sources.title: LEQEMBI Subcutaneous Autoinjector Clinical Data Supports Similar Efficacy and Safety to IV Formulation in Early Alzheimer's Disease Presented at AAIC 2026
